questions.q: What was the peaceful 1989 revolution that ended communist rule called?
questions.why: Students and artists led the protests.

questions.q: What was the 1968 period of reform crushed by Warsaw Pact tanks called?
questions.why: Alexander Dubček led it.

questions.q: Who was Czechoslovakia's first President, in 1918?
questions.why: He is called the father of the nation.

questions.q: Which Holy Roman Emperor made Prague a great capital in the 1300s?
questions.why: Charles Bridge and Charles University are named after him.

questions.q: Which reformer was burned at the stake in 1415?
questions.why: His followers were the Hussites.

questions.q: Which 1618 event in Prague started the Thirty Years' War?
questions.why: Officials were thrown from a castle window.

questions.q: Which 1938 agreement gave the Sudetenland to Germany?
questions.why: Czechoslovakia was not invited.

questions.q: Which student set himself on fire in 1969 to protest the occupation?
questions.why: A square in Prague is named after him.

questions.q: Which 1620 battle ended Bohemian independence for centuries?
questions.why: It came early in the Thirty Years' War.

questions.q: Which 1805 battle was fought near Brno?
questions.why: Napoleon won his greatest victory there.

questions.q: Which Czech monk discovered the laws of heredity in Brno?
questions.why: He worked with pea plants.

questions.q: Which medieval clock on Prague's Old Town Hall shows moving apostles?
questions.why: It was first installed in 1410.

questions.q: What is the capital of Czechia?
questions.why: It is called the 'City of a Hundred Spires'.

questions.q: Which pale lager is named after a Czech city?
questions.why: It was first brewed in Plzeň in 1842.

questions.q: Which river flows through Prague?
questions.why: Smetana wrote a famous piece about it.

questions.q: Which runner, the 'Czech Locomotive', won three golds at Helsinki 1952?
questions.why: He won the 5,000 m, 10,000 m and marathon.

questions.q: Which tennis player born in Prague won 18 Grand Slam singles titles?
questions.why: She won Wimbledon nine times.

questions.q: Which composer wrote the 'New World Symphony'?
questions.why: He wrote it in the USA in 1893.

questions.q: Which spa town hosts an international film festival?
questions.why: It is famous for its hot springs.

questions.q: Which playwright became President after the 1989 revolution?
questions.why: Prague's airport is named after him.

questions.q: Which Czech author wrote 'The Metamorphosis'?
questions.why: He wrote in German.

questions.q: Which Czech writer coined the word 'robot'?
questions.why: It appeared in his 1920 play 'R.U.R.'.

questions.q: Which writer wrote 'The Unbearable Lightness of Being'?
questions.why: It is set during the Prague Spring.

questions.q: Which emperor made Prague a centre of art and alchemy around 1600?
questions.why: Astronomers Tycho Brahe and Kepler worked for him.

questions.q: Which medieval bridge in Prague is lined with statues?
questions.why: Building began in 1357.

questions.q: In which year did Czechoslovakia split into two countries?
questions.why: The 'Velvet Divorce' was peaceful.

questions.q: Which saint and duke of Bohemia is honoured in a Christmas carol?
questions.why: He is the 'Good King Wenceslas'.

questions.q: What is Czechia's currency?
questions.why: It means 'crown'.

questions.q: Which castle complex in Prague is one of the largest in the world?
questions.why: It holds St Vitus Cathedral.

questions.q: Which bone church near Kutná Hora is decorated with human bones?
questions.why: About 40,000 skeletons were used.
